title: Seedkit Onboard: Surgeon Snips & Pricing Angles
summary: A compact playbook for a tiny 'seedkit' onboarding flow aimed at engineers who want the fastest path from try to measurable traction. Focus: 90s to first successful call, transparent cost framing, and three short pricing language variants to A/B in the sign-up funnel.
content:
Context:
This doc collects microcopy, quickstart steps, and pricing phrasing designed for an extremely compact experiential funnel ("seedkit") that we plan to run as a rapid experiment for Hosted API onboarding. Target user: engineer building an internal prototype or POC (not enterprise buying lead).

Design goals:
- Get a working generate/embedding call in <=90s with minimal friction.
- Make cost expectations explicit at the moment of first call (avoid surprise billing).
- Surface a clear upgrade trigger (when they hit X tokens or X queries).
- Use developer-first language: technical examples, shell snippets, curl-first.

Quickstart flow (90s):
1) Landing CTA: "Try a 1-minute inference — no credit card" (button)
2) Instant sandbox token issued, ephemeral policy, 1,000 free tokens or 30 queries.
3) Inline console with sample prompt + curl + JS SDK snippet visible side-by-side.
4) First call runs and returns a streaming response; UX shows estimated tokens used and dollar-equivalent for that single call (rounded).
5) Post-call microcopy: "This call used ~12 tokens (~$0.00048). Keep testing free up to 1,000 tokens. Save your token to persist your project."

Snippets to show (short, copy-first):
- curl (copyable):
  curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SEEDKIT' \\n       -d '{"model":"rwft-1-small","input":"Summarize the following: ..."}' \\n       https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

- Node (2 lines):
  const r = await Redwood.generate({ model: 'rwft-1-small', input: 'Write a subject line for...' });

Pricing-language variants (three short experiments):
A — Transparent per-call: "Pay per token. This demo uses ~12 tokens (~$0.0005). Live pricing: $0.002 / 1k tokens for small models — scale pricing available."
B — Usage bands + frictionless upgrade: "Start free (1k tokens). After free, switch to pay-as-you-go: $0.002 / 1k tokens. Predictable: add reserved capacity when you need consistent throughput."
C — Developer-first microcost framing: "Each sample call is pennies. Typical prototype uses ~500 tokens/day (~$0.001). If you move to production, we help set a committed pool for predictable unit cost."

Microcopy rules (tone + examples):
- Keep sentences short, technical, and to-the-point. Avoid marketing fluff.
- Use explicit numeric examples for a single sample call.
- When mentioning price, show both per-token and a relatable per-day prototype figure.
- Provide next-steps as code snippets and a single CTA: "Persist token & connect repo".

Competitive note (short):
- Competitor A focuses on "one-liner simplicity" but hides per-token math; engineers hit surprise bills.
- Competitor B gives large free quotas but requires credit card to upgrade; friction when projects move from POC to team usage.
- Our angle: developer-first clarity + immediate observability of token/dollar cost inline. That differentiator resonates with engineers building prototypes with limited budgets.

Risks / objections we should prewrite for support and sales: 
- "Why is there a hard cap on free tokens?" -> reply: "Caps prevent expensive model abuse during open sandboxing; we surface cheap model variants and auto-fallbacks to keep iteration cheap."
- "What if I need to test at scale?" -> reply: "Quick path: convert to dev credentials and spin a small Dedicated commit; we provide ramp guides and tooling to simulate production throughput."

Metrics to measure in the experiment (primary + secondary):
- Primary: % of seeded signups that make a successful first API call (target 45%+).
- Secondary: conversion to saved token/project within 7 days (target 15%), average tokens used in first week, NPS from post-experience micro-survey.

A/B test matrix (minimal):
- Variant X: Pricing copy A vs B vs C (on checkout modal)
- Variant Y: Console-first vs Code-first layout (which snippet is prominent)
- Variant Z: Free tokens: 1k vs 2.5k (impact on conversion vs cost)

Implementation notes for product/engineers:
- Quick analytics hook: emit event when first call completes with tokens_estimate, model, and ephemeral_token_flag.
- Console should call cost-estimator microservice to show per-call $-estimate before execution.
- Rate-limit seed tokens aggressively and allow extensible lift via simple form (email + project reason).

Open questions / decisions required:
- Default model for seedkit: rwft-1-small vs rwft-1-medium? (trade-off cost vs perceived quality)
- Exact free token amount (1k recommended but test 2.5k)
- Should we require email to persist token or allow anonymous persisted projects?

Next steps (for this doc):
- Finalize two short microcopy variants for landing + post-call messages (Ravi) — due EOD next Tuesday.
- Product to prototype console layout with inline cost estimate (Liam) — spike 3 days.
- Growth to wire funnel for A/Bing pricing copy (Sofia) — plan for 2-week experiment.

Quick paste-ready microcopy candidates (pick one set per experiment):
- Landing headline: "Make your first inference in 60s — no credit card."
- Post-call success: "Nice! That call used ~12 tokens (~$0.0005). You have 988 free tokens left. Persist your token to keep this project."
- Upgrade modal short: "Keep building: pay-as-you-go from $0.002 / 1k tokens. Need predictability? Consider reserved capacity for steady workloads."

Notes to self: keep phrasing concrete, engineer-first, and instrumentable. Avoid aspirational claims like "enterprise-grade" in the seedkit funnel. The product should sell itself via low-friction magic: code + cost clarity.
